body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (0) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📎 Requirement gaps (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Large stored IDs make edits crash ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 41f5b75

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>Added MAX_ID = 2**63 - 1 in todo/store.py and _is_item_id bounds stored IDs to 1..MAX_ID; _valid now
>requires next_id <= MAX_ID + 1, so oversized IDs/next_id are rejected as StoreError at load, before
>any save. _cmd_add in todo/cli.py refuses to append when next_id exceeds MAX_ID (WriteError), so the
>repaired counter can never grow past a serializable size. Tests cover huge IDs and next_id values
>being rejected. This is a different implementation from the suggested fix (bound-based validation
>rather than a serialization check at save time), but it addresses the same crash by ensuring every
>saved integer stays within a safe size.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>load repairs next_id by adding one to the largest stored ID without checking whether that result
>can be serialized. If a hand-edited file contains a valid 4,300-digit item ID and a smaller
>next_id, the repaired counter has 4,301 digits; subsequent add, done, or remove saves raise
>an uncaught ValueError during JSON serialization.
>
>
2. New items can receive unusable negative IDs ✓ Resolved

Resolving commit: 41f5b75

>
>Resolution reason >
> >
>_fresh_id now floors at 1 via max([0] + ...), and _valid_item/_is_item_id reject item IDs below 1 at
>load time, so negative-ID items cannot be saved by add. Tests added for negative item IDs raising
>StoreError.
>
>
>
>Description >
> >
>_fresh_id adds one to the highest stored ID but does not enforce its stated minimum of 1. With a
>hand-edited file whose item IDs and next_id are negative, add can save another negative ID that
>the new done and remove commands reject as an argument.
>
>

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
